summary.title: Honeypot Deployment: Threat Model
summary.description: This threat model covers a network-based honeypot deployed to detect and analyze unauthorized access attempts. The primary concern in scope is containment: if an attacker who compromises the honeypot is able to move laterally into other parts of the network, this could expose production systems, internal credentials, or sensitive data, potentially leading to broader compromise of the organization's infrastructure. The model evaluates the honeypot's network segmentation, monitoring, and isolation controls to assess how well it prevents this kind of pivot.

threats.title: No MFA org Router SSH
threats.description: The organisation router's management SSH has no MFA, allowing credential-based compromise of routing configuration.
threats.mitigation: Enforce MFA on router management; use key-based auth over passwords

threats.title: Org Router Firewall Misconfiguration
threats.description: Misconfigured firewall rules on the Org Router could allow attacker traffic broader access into the internal network than intended, undermining the first layer of perimeter defense.
threats.mitigation: Regularly audit firewall rulesets; apply default-deny with explicit allow rules only for required traffic

threats.title: No MFA on L2 Switch Management SSH
threats.description: The L2 switch's management SSH interface lacks MFA, risking unauthorized configuration changes if credentials are compromised.
threats.mitigation: Enforce MFA on switch management access; restrict to IT or VLAN only

threats.title: Honeypot Fingerprinting
threats.description: Undiscovered weaknesses (VM artifacts, inconsistent service banners, unnatural traffic patterns) could allow an attacker to determine the system is a honeypot rather than a real production host.
threats.mitigation: Harden honeypot to reduce detectable artifacts; monitor for reconnaissance behaviour indicating fingerprinting attempts

threats.title: Fingerprinting-Driven False Telemetry / Mitigation Gap
threats.description: Once the attacker recognises the honeypot, they may feed deliberately false or misleading behaviour into it. The organisation's resulting mitigations (based on this poisoned data) may leave a predictable, known gap the attacker can later exploit.
threats.mitigation: Cross-validate honeypot findings against independent detection sources (e.g. compare Suricata vs. Zeek results) before acting on them; treat honeypot data as a signal, not sole justification, for mitigation decisions

data.name: Decoy PC
data.description: This PC allows for us to see the attacker's lateral movement within the Honeypot VLAN

threats.title: No MFA on L3 Switch Management SSH
threats.description: The L3 switch's management SSH interface has no MFA, allowing an attacker who obtains credentials to log in and alter routing/ACL configuration.
threats.mitigation: Enforce MFA on switch management access; restrict management interface to an out-of-band network

threats.title: Routig Table Exposure via L3 Switch
threats.description: Exploiting the L3 switch's management interface could allow an attacker to view routing tables, revealing the existence and IP addressing of the Production VLAN.
threats.mitigation: Restrict management interface access; disable unnecessary services that could leak routing data

threats.title: ACL and Firewall Misconfiguration Enabling Boundary Crossing
threats.description: Improperly configured ACLs and firewalls at the L3 switch boundary could allow an attacker with routing knowledge to cross from the Honeypot zone into the Protected Asset Zone
threats.mitigation: Regularly audit and test ACL rules; apply least-privilege segmentation between VLANs

data.name: Honeypot Logs
data.description: All attacker TTPs gathered from the honeypot using SPAN Mirroring

threats.title: Honeypot Log tampering
threats.description: If an attacker pivots into the Monitoring VLAN (via a boundary failure), they could alter or delete stored logs to erase evidence of their activity, directly undermining the research dataset.
threats.mitigation: Write-once/append-only log storage; separate log storage host from analysis host; regular integrity hashing of log files

threats.title: Traffic Tampering in Transit
threats.description: Traffic between router and switch could be altered if an attacker gains a foothold on either device, injecting malicious payloads downstream.
threats.mitigation: Integrity monitoring on internal links; segment management traffic from data traffic

threats.title: Unathorised Inter Switch Traffic
threats.description: Malformed or unauthorized traffic between switches could exploit trunk misconfiguration, enabling VLAN hopping.
threats.mitigation: Disable unused trunk ports; explicitly define allowed VLANs per trunk

threats.title: Undecrypted Data link b
threats.description: Log data could be read en route from the Honeypot process to the Monitoring VLAN if no form of data ecyrption in trnasit exists
threats.mitigation: Encrypt data in transit using strong encryption standards

threats.title: Production Network Compromise
threats.description: If the attacker successfully crosses the boundary, they can access sensitive company data, escalate privileges, and potentially disrupt or cripple production systems.
threats.mitigation: Defense-in-depth: network segmentation, monitoring alerts on cross-VLAN traffic, incident response plan for breach containment
